sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: ENS is a small, predominantly project-based digital-commerce and software-services company, not an established subscription-software compounder. sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
ENS Enterprises Limited; ISIN INE23ER01017; BSE SME code 544876; NSE interoperability symbol ENS$ is not an NSE operating listing. Incorporated 7 January 2016, converted to public limited 8 May 2025; same standalone legal entity, no consolidated subsidiary results used. Financial basis: Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, restated audited FY2024–FY2026, with original FY2021/FY2022 and restated FY2023 extension. Latest audited period 31 March 2026; no verified September 2026 results or current cash-flow statement located. Cutoff 20 October 2026. Price ₹105.80 is secondary dated 19 October close/last trade, not a live executable bid. Current shares 1,35,94,912 give market capitalization ₹143.83 crore. Five-year nominal INR returns before personal tax; equity hurdle 15%, sensitivity 12%/18%. Analytical operating-capital opportunity-cost range 13%–18% is separate, not a substitute equity hurdle. Liquidity reference ₹5lakh is analytical, not a suitable allocation recommendation.

G1 Conditional, with capital-allocation/control concerns but no evidenced fraud or diversion. G2 Hold — unresolved because three full years lacked an audit trail and certain financial-note differences remain unexplained. G3 Hold — unresolved because actual post-IPO cash/deployment and renewal are not confirmed; no claim of actual insolvency. G4 Hold — unresolved because trade restrictions, spread and actual BSE traded values are not confirmed. Confidence is High in exact identity, issued shares/lot and transcription of audited totals; Medium in economic comparability and current valuation inputs; Low in marginal returns, post-IPO execution, current funding and executability. Documentary numerical precision is not the same as confidence in future economics.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV4, MOAT4, REV8, DUR4, CAP NS, CASH2, BAL4, EXEC NS, EARN6. IAS factors R NS, D3, P4, L NS. Each has two material supporting facts, a contrary fact, evidence IDs and confidence in factor_audit. Unknown execution or capital returns are not filled with 5.

BQS known weighted sum 3.48; scoreable coverage 80%; missing weight 20%; mathematical raw bound 3.68–5.48. GQS (Growth Quality Score) known sum 5.10; coverage 85%; raw bound 5.25–6.60. Persistent poor cash realization (CASH2, four-year CFO/PAT0.14×) triggers the permitted GQS≤5 cap. GQS remains NS, even though the capped mathematical bound is 5–5. This is not a rankable 5. IAS known contribution D0.60+P0.40=1.00; direct coverage 30%; generic missing bound 1.70–8.00. Propagating the underlying BQS bound exactly once tightens IAS to 2.37–6.87. Neither bound is a statistical interval or a ranking substitute.

No governance or funding-failure cap applies. G3 Hold alone does not exclude a company from quality ranking: here CAP/EXEC missingness prevents a complete BQS and CAP missingness prevents GQS, while financial-reliability uncertainty independently matters. Moving the two uncertain scored judgments GOV and DUR together±1 moves BQS bounds±0.30 and IAS quality contribution±0.075; no NS midpoint is invented. REV starts at 9 for≥30% CAGR, uses a ceiling 8 for comparability/confidence rather than an extra small-base penalty, and gets no trajectory/TAM bonus.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
ENS develops and integrates e-commerce systems, digital storefronts, software, cloud/DevOps and related services. Its claimed Shopify/Google/ONDC affiliations can help distribution, but certifications and partner labels are not exclusivity or a royalty moat. FY2026 revenue ₹51.373 crore comprised ₹39.467 crore one-time project fees and ₹11.907 crore recurring retainers; subscription-based revenue was explicitly zero in each of FY2024–FY2026. Recurring fees are not automatically ARR, net revenue retention or SaaS subscriptions. The risk and business sections describe customer dependence and lack of long-term/exclusive contractual protection. No audited customer cohort retention, churn, CAC or lifetime contribution is disclosed.

Domestic revenue ₹45.694 crore was 88.95% of FY2026; exports ₹5.679 crore were 11.05%. ONDC contributed only ₹0.6265 crore,1.22%, down 8.24% year-on-year, so it cannot explain overall growth. Management claims 4,200+ projects for 3,100+ clients over the company's life, but that is not current active clients or independently verified retention. Outsourced/direct service cost ₹28.542 crore consumed 55.56% ofsales before employee cost ₹7.766 crore. Cash is collected through customer/project arrangements while vendors, payroll and statutory balances must be funded. No proven gross/net principal-agent bridge is available for the changing service mix; retain audited gross revenue and show retained-value cross-checks separately.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is accumulated implementation experience and customer relationships, which may lower acquisition friction and support follow-on work. Evidence against a structural moat is the one-time revenue mix, lack of verified pricing power or exclusivity, zero subscription sales and concentrated counterparties. FY2026 top customer was 18.85%, top-three 37.25%, top-five 49.32%, top-ten 69.17%; the top customer concentration improved from 63.67%FY2024, but top-ten rose from 60.12%FY2025. Top-ten suppliers were 90.88% of cost-of-services purchases; top-three 62.93%. Supplier identities/beneficial ownership were not supplied in the reviewed table. That is a verification gap, not an allegation of related-party billing. AI tools may aid delivery while commoditizing routine work; a proprietary cost or switching advantage has not been quantified.

Peers are economic cross-checks, not an automatic valuation basket. InfoBeans FY2026 standalone revenue/PAT/CFO were ₹381.08/67.07/21.83 crore, so CFO/PAT0.33×; Silver Touch was ₹315.131/37.769/19.919 crore,0.53×. ENS was ₹51.373/8.398/−1.100 crore,−0.13×. Larger scale and different geographic mix, hardware/system-integration content, leases and Ind AS treatment prevent naive margin comparisons. ASM is a third, more distant engineering/manufacturing comparator: ENS's prospectus states FY2026 standalone revenue ₹479.786 crore and EBITDA ₹95.015 crore; the official ASM index was found, but its report download was unavailable, so these are not independently normalized peer numbers. No current peer P/E is claimed. The base terminal 12× operating NOPAT is an analytical assumption tested at 8×/10×/15×, not a disguised observed peer multiple.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue rose from ₹1.112934 crore FY2021 to ₹3.126249FY2022,₹7.355353FY2023,₹10.109205FY2024,₹28.333347FY2025 and ₹51.373180FY2026. Six annual observations support a five-year CAGR115.2%; the comparable restated FY2023–FY2026 three-year CAGR is 91.2%. Ten-year CAGR is ND. Annual additions were ₹2.0133,₹4.2291,₹2.7539,₹18.2241 and ₹23.0398 crore, respectively. FY2026 growth was 81.3%, slower than FY2025's 180.3%, but an impressive absolute increase. No acquisitions are disclosed in the historical standalone perimeter; precise organic price/volume/currency attribution remains unavailable.

Revenue minus cost of services, before employees, increased ₹7.2921→₹15.2643→₹22.8308 crore FY2024–FY2026, about 76.9% two-year CAGR, below gross-sales 125.4%. This proxy is not accounting gross profit because employee delivery cost remains below it. FY2026 direct costs rose faster than revenue; retained value grew 49.6% versus reported 81.3%. This is a substantive cross-check of activity expansion without awarding software-like economics to outsourced revenue. FY2021/FY2022 are original audited rather than IPO-restated; original/restated differences in later employee provisions, tax and share count are disclosed, not silently blended. No current quarter or half-year was annualized. September 2025 interim in the draft is historical and superseded by FY2026, not a current TTM update.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The growth route is to add specialized AI, data, product and sales capability and better infrastructure. It is not a free software capacity expansion. Net IPO proceeds ₹29.8721 crore allocate ₹17.02 crore to 65 hires,₹6.7521 crore to IT,₹1.20 crore repayment and ₹4.90 crore GCP. The hiring table is annual CTC: four top-management roles ₹3.4 crore,30R&D ₹8.6 crore, four product ₹1.4 crore,18sales ₹2.97 crore, support ₹0.20 crore, HR ₹0.30 crore, finance ₹0.15 crore. Annual software ₹4.7537 crore plus 2% vendor charge makes ₹4.8488 crore recurring cost; only ₹1.9984 crore hardware is modeled as growth capex. Recruitment fees reconstructed from disclosed brackets are ₹1.37395 crore one-off, with ₹1.21538 crore hardware/software GST timing reserve. Input-credit recovery is an assumption, not free cash. These amounts are not deducted again as IPO capital expenditure after appearing in operating cash flow.

At unchanged FY2026 contribution after direct services 44.44%, the incremental recurring payroll/software bill ₹21.869 crore needs roughly ₹49.21 crore incremental annual revenue merely to cover itself, before additional overhead, capex, tax and working capital. The model's total first-year break-even is higher because existing salaries/overheads also inflate. This scale is economically meaningful relative to existing ₹51.37 crore sales and requires actual contract wins and cash collection, not a generic global TAM. Existing headcount declined 140FY2025→127FY2026→100 June 2026, so the 65-hire plan is a capability/mix change, not a straightforward extrapolation of historical productivity.

Accounting operating IC, after stripping cash, financial investments and ICD and consistently including operating deposits, rose from ₹0.5584 crore FY2023 to ₹1.7031FY2024,₹7.0782FY2025 and ₹15.7707FY2026. FY2026 accounting ROIC proxy 72.3% and one-year ΔNOPAT/ΔIC52.1% are retained only as arithmetic diagnostics. They do not establish returns on additional capital: much human/software investment is expensed, client mix changes, and customer/vendor float dominates the denominator. There is no meaningful incremental project/cohort return, retention-adjusted payback, contribution or acquisition-cost series to substitute. CAP is NS, not 5 or an extrapolated high ROCE. Against a reasoned 13%–18% nominal capital-cost range, the marginal spread is unknown. GQS stays NS with the cash-quality cap separately shown.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters include Manish Kumar Srivastava (whole-time director/CFO), Avinash Kumar Singh (chairman), and Anupam Kumar Srivastava, who resigned as whole-time director on 1 December 2025 but remains a promoter shareholder. Promoter/group shares of 7,494,390 divided by 13,594,912 current shares calculate to 55.1264%. Small printed percentage differences are not preferred to exact share counts. The issue had no OFS, but ownership alone does not establish alignment. March 2025 rights proceeds of ₹4.4005 crore and subsequent bonus issues are separate: bonus shares are not economic dilution, whereas the fresh IPO dilutes existing holders' percentage by 26.5%. No outstanding options, warrants or convertibles were disclosed. Latest pledge and encumbrance changes still need verification.

Capital allocation is a concern. ₹6.0321 crore invested in Macobs shares and a ₹2.7281 crore unsecured ICD to ACME Corporate Advisors coexist with negative operating cash and demand debt. The ICD contract describes ₹2.50 crore at 10%, with quarterly interest; maturity and the closing-balance reconciliation require evidence. Similar ACME names among advisers/investors do not prove the borrower is related. FY2026 related director remuneration totals ₹0.8625 crore in the RPT note versus ₹0.85422 crore in the expense note, an unresolved ₹0.00828 crore difference. Relative remuneration of ₹0.3375 crore and director payables of ₹0.42316 crore warrant review, not double counting.

Tally application/database audit trails were disabled throughout April 2023–March 2026, and the auditor could not comment on tampering. This is an evidenced control deficiency, not evidence that tampering occurred. TDS of ₹0.6354 crore was outstanding and in the process of deposit. Tax proceedings summarize ₹0.058254 crore direct and ₹0.803941 crore GST demands, with narrative unit differences and possible overlap with recorded balances. Auditor resignations in 2023 and 2025 cite preoccupation; no dispute is assumed. The unqualified restated opinion does not cure the absent audit trail.

Promises versus delivery: the IPO is completed and reflected in the exchange master. Hiring planned for August 2026–January 2027 and IT installation by December 2026 were not yet due at cutoff; completion was not verified. Hiring/software quotations are not placed orders. Expired quotation validity is not a contract default. The new capital program cannot receive an execution score from intentions alone, so EXEC is NS. Sample-PDF and Exato-labelled links on the investor site were rejected, not attributed to ENS. This access-date source defect is not presented as a proven pre-cutoff regulatory violation.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY2024/25/26 PAT was ₹0.9032/3.7040/8.3981 crore; operating EBIT excluding all other income was ₹1.2225/5.0482/11.1662 crore. Normalized PAT subtracts other income after an illustrative 26% tax, giving ₹0.8921/3.4949/8.1074 crore. Ordinary payroll, software, listing, recruitment, CSR and bad-debt costs are not added back. FY2025 other income included a ₹0.2722 crore liability writeback; FY2026 included ₹0.2585 interest, ₹0.1331 FX and ₹0.0011 securities gain. The FY2026 tax charge includes a ₹0.1944 crore deferred-tax credit. Prospective cash tax uses 26% on positive earnings after interest, without an immediate tax refund for losses.

The FY2026 CFO bridge begins with PBT ₹11.4160 crore, adds D&A ₹0.5388 and interest ₹0.1429, and removes interest income ₹0.2585, FX ₹0.1331 and securities gain ₹0.0011: ₹11.7050 crore before working capital. AR absorbs ₹5.8128, other current assets ₹3.6532 and payables ₹5.0624; other liabilities add ₹3.4574 and provisions ₹1.4780. Cash generated ₹2.1120 less reported tax ₹3.2123 gives CFO −₹1.1004. This is a collections/vendor-funding issue, not caused by the ₹0.0272 crore capex. Opening cash ₹1.6165 + CFO −1.1004 + CFI −4.0247 + CFF 3.8225 reconciles closing ₹0.3139 within rounding. Four-year CFO ₹1.9003 versus PAT ₹13.5610 gives 0.140×, with FCF proxy ₹0.2549 after ₹1.6455 cash capex.

AR of ₹17.1075 crore includes ₹2.6032 crore overdue beyond six months, with no doubtful provision disclosed. Average AR days increased from 84.9 to 100.4, although ending AR days improved from 143.8 to 121.5. Vendor advances of ₹5.3948 crore need recovery/delivery evidence. Trade payables fell from ₹6.7881 to ₹1.7257 crore, reversing supplier funding. The no-MSME-dues assertion depends on supplier information, not independent verification. Customer advances of ₹2.8549 crore are inside operating working capital, not free cash added separately.

The opening-claims ledger routes every item once. Old GST/TDS/EPF/ESIC of ₹1.714522 crore is removed from operating float and paid once. Net income tax ₹1.979081 and current employee provisions ₹0.032693 are paid once; long employee provisions ₹0.60458 are deducted at terminal. Demand debt ₹3.965405 is repaid in year one, including the ₹1.20 crore IPO object, not in addition to it. Macobs and ICD recoveries enter terminal assets only, not funding cash or operating earnings. Term deposits ₹0.124157 are excluded pending availability evidence. Operating rent remains in operating expenses; no synthetic Ind AS lease liability is invented. The annual table, original/restated reconciliation, and return/working-capital formulae accompany the report.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹105.80 and 13,594,912 shares, market capitalization is ₹143.8342 crore. FY2026 PAT divided by current shares gives EPS ₹6.18 and historical P/E 17.13×. Using pre-IPO EPS ₹8.40 would incorrectly show 12.60×. Normalized P/E 17.74×, March-balance P/B 7.80×, and reported FCF yield −0.78% are cross-checks, not intrinsic values. Current EV cannot be asserted without post-IPO cash. Explicit March-no-IPO EV is ₹147.61 crore, about 12.61× operating EBITDA. Full-net-IPO pro-forma P/B of approximately 2.98× assumes funds retained and excludes intervening results; it is not observed book value.

The reproducible five-year model includes recurring hiring/software, direct service costs, working capital, capex, recruitment, GST timing, taxes, claim settlement and full initial bank repayment. Starting resources are the March available-cash proxy ₹0.1897 plus full net IPO ₹29.8721, not verified October cash. Annual periods end on 19 October 2027–2031. FY2026 is the scale anchor, not an assertion that fiscal and model periods coincide. The full-rollout case uses fully annual new costs in year one, with 50%/75% first-year ramps separately tested. There are no interim dividends; terminal cash is counted once. Annual 0.5% dilution is illustrative, not disclosed warrants.

Bear: growth −25%, 5%, 8%, 10%, 10%; direct cost 60% of sales; ONWC 42%; terminal 8× NOPAT; 25% nonoperating-asset recovery. New staffing/software are partly curtailed after year one. A first-year shortfall and peak ₹51.78 crore gap make ordinary IRR null. A separate discounted-equity rescue is uncommitted, not an ordinary return. Base: growth 25%, 20%, 18%, 15%, 12%; FY2026 direct-cost ratio 55.56%; ONWC 33%; 12× NOPAT; 60% asset recovery. Terminal price ₹75.08, IRR −6.63%, minimum cash ₹1.46 crore. Bull: growth 45%, 35%, 25%, 20%, 15%; direct cost 50%; ONWC 28%; 15× NOPAT; 85% recovery. Terminal price ₹423.29 and IRR 31.96%. Bull requires faster growth and better delivery economics simultaneously; no subjective probability-weighted IRR is supplied.

At 12× NOPAT, the 15% hurdle requires constant 25.86% revenue growth to ₹162.25 crore and an 18.86% terminal EBIT margin, with funding intact. Terminal multiples 8×/10×/12×/15× and hurdles 12%/15%/18% are solved explicitly. The two-way growth/multiple grid keeps unfunded cases null. The funded base conditional entry price is ₹37.33 for a 15% hurdle, about ₹32.82–₹42.60 for 18%/12%. This is an assumption-dependent range, not a buy recommendation or observable fair value. A ₹5 crore unverified intervening cash drain creates a ₹3.54 crore base funding gap and null ordinary IRR. Collection losses and 0%/1%/3%/5% each-way execution costs are also tested. Actual opening resources and cost implementation remain unverified, so R is NS rather than any illustrative return being treated as supported.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that all sales are fictitious. It is that real delivery growth absorbs cash in receivables/vendor advances while the company builds an expensive capability base before cash-paying demand matures. Losing the largest customer, 18.85% of sales, plus pressure on other projects can reduce contribution while fixed personnel costs persist. A 25% sales shock covers that customer loss plus second-order weakness; ONWC rising to 42% from the base 33% links collection and vendor stress. Unplaced hiring/software can be paused, and investments might be recovered. These are material mitigants, but not committed cash.

Permanent-loss risk is High. Funded base terminal price is 29.0% below entry before costs. The unfunded bear has no ordinary price-return claim. The separate hypothetical rescue issues new equity at a 40% discount to entry to fund deficits, explicitly diluting existing holders. Failure to clear statutory dues, fix audit controls or avoid verified diversion would matter more than quote volatility. Contrary evidence is genuine historical growth, positive prior-year CFO and the substantial IPO raise. The decisive thesis variable is cash contribution generated by the new cost base, verified through collections rather than sales recognition alone.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
No multibagger designation is supported. A 5× price in five years requires 38.0% annual price growth; 10× requires 58.5%. Over ten years, the respective requirements are 17.5% and 25.9%. The accompanying decomposition fixes terminal PAT margin at 12%, annual dilution at 0.5%, and lower terminal P/E multiples of 10×/12× instead of assuming unlimited rerating.

At 12× P/E, a 5× five-year price requires approximately ₹61.4 crore PAT and ₹512 crore annual revenue; 10× requires approximately ₹122.9 crore PAT and ₹1,024 crore revenue. These are roughly 10×/20× today's sales, with ₹169/₹338 crore working capital at 33%, before fixed investment and extra staffing/software. Exact results and ten-year variants are retained in the model. There is no reliable accessible-market denominator or demonstrated customer/cohort path supporting these outcomes. Funding and dilution cannot be assumed away. Classification: speculative/unsupported, not impossible and not a probability forecast.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
These are research checkpoints, not automations or trade instructions:
1. Cash and IPO use: reconcile gross ₹33.1421 crore through expenses and actual utilization to dated bank balances. An unexplained ₹1.5 crore drain matters against the illustrative base cushion. Missing evidence keeps G3/R on hold.
2. Collections: March AR ₹17.1075 crore, over-six-month overdue ₹2.6032 crore. Investigate ageing above ₹3 crore or average AR days above 120; repeated nonpayment requiring rescue is a potential thesis break.
3. Cash conversion: four-year CFO/PAT is 0.14×. Require actual cash-flow statements and a commercial explanation for improvement. One temporary working-capital release is not durable conversion.
4. Hiring/software: compare 65 hires, ₹17.02 crore annual payroll and ₹4.85 crore annual software with December 2026/January 2027 milestones, actual costs and paying contracts. A milestone not yet due is not yet missed.
5. CAP: obtain project-vintage contribution, retention, acquisition cost and cash payback before assigning a score. Aggregate ROCE cannot clear this gap.
6. Controls: verify audit trails enabled and retained, TDS cleared, and GST/direct-tax claims reconciled without overlap. Material unresolved controls keep G2 on hold.
7. Noncore assets: verify Macobs quantity/value and ICD borrower, maturity and collections. Further noncore allocation during cash stress is an alert, not automatic proof of abuse.
8. Funding: verify ICICI renewal or repayment and conditions. Do not treat the difference between limit and borrowing as available liquidity.
9. Ownership/execution: verify pledges, lock-ins, surveillance, spreads and actual BSE traded values. The 1,200-share lot makes small-position liquidity nonlinear. Refresh before implementation.
10. Earnings: separate one-time, recurring and subscription sales; include the new expense base and use current/fully diluted shares, not pre-IPO weighted averages.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved / insufficient evidence. Research priority is cash, controls and marginal economics before price. No BQS/GQS/IAS point score or numerical rank is warranted. Poor cash conversion is evidenced; CAP/EXEC/R/L are missing-evidence NS, not low or neutral imputations. This is not Avoid — governance because material diversion is not established, and not Distressed/funding failure because modeled stress and unverified renewal are not an actual default. G3 Hold alone is not used to reject business quality.

At the dated ₹105.80 price, the funded conditional base is 21.6 percentage points below the 15% hurdle. However, R remains NS without current resources and cost-ramp verification. A cheaper share price cannot repair an unfunded operating plan. The company is not eligible for investment consideration until critical gates and marginal-economics gaps are cleared. If already held, this is a review candidate for cash/control/execution/liquidity reasons, not an automatic exit instruction. Position size, taxes and real market depth would matter. No allocation or trade is authorized or executed.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Every material finding has source IDs and page-level locators. Final prospectus S1 supersedes older financial values where available; S2 supplies FY2023 restatement; S3/S4 extend annual history without treating old EPS as bonus-adjusted comparable. Audited P&L, cash flow, investments and control disclosures were visually checked against extracted text. The June website restatement is archived, but the July 17 report inside the final August prospectus controls. Secondary prices and placeholder PDFs are not upgraded to primary evidence.

Open questions: actual cash and IPO use, bank renewal, cohort returns, staffing/software implementation, contracted coverage, aged AR and vendor advances, ICD terms and recovery, Macobs realizable value, RPT pay differences, audit-trail remediation, tax overlap, and current pledges/surveillance/spreads. Official BSE quote/RTA downloads failed with HTTP 403. Absence from NSE trading archives is not a zero trade for a BSE security. Only 40 listed sessions had elapsed; no pre-listing zero rows are manufactured. No located credit rating means ND, not an investment-grade assumption.

Editable assumptions include 26% tax; 13%–18% capital-cost comparison; separate 15% equity hurdle; five years; 0.5% annual dilution; no interim dividends; fully annual new costs with ramp alternatives; 5% cost inflation; 33% base ONWC; 12× terminal NOPAT; and 60% financial-asset recovery. Scripts reproduce the financial and liquidity calculations. Source-document changes after 20 October are not used as new operating information. This research is not an investment recommendation.

GOV.reason: Material stewardship and control concerns without proven diversion or minority abuse. No governance override.
supporting_facts: Noncore Macobs investment ₹6.03 crore and unsecured ICD ₹2.73 crore coexist with negative CFO and debt.
Audit trails were disabled for three financial years; ₹0.6354 crore TDS awaited deposit.
GOV.contrary_fact: No OFS, no disclosed related-party loans, and an unqualified restated opinion. Auditor resignations cite preoccupation, not a proven dispute.

MOAT.reason: Useful delivery relationships, but no demonstrated structural barrier.
supporting_facts: Subscription revenue is zero; 76.8% of FY2026 sales were one-time fees.
Top ten customers contributed 69.17%; top ten vendors supplied 90.88% of direct service costs.
MOAT.contrary_fact: Recurring revenue rose from ₹4.727 to ₹11.907 crore and largest-customer concentration declined.

REV.reason: The five-year reported CAGR starts at 9 under the rubric; a confidence/comparability ceiling of 8 applies. No extra small-base penalty or trajectory bonus.
supporting_facts: Six audited annual observations support a 115.2% five-year CAGR; three-year CAGR is 91.2%.
Retained value before employees rose from ₹7.292 to ₹22.831 crore in FY2024–FY2026.
REV.contrary_fact: Direct service costs rose from 27.9% to 55.6% of revenue, and ONDC revenue declined in FY2026.

DUR.reason: Demand exists, but the higher-cost expansion has no verified contracted coverage.
supporting_facts: ₹39.47 crore FY2026 revenue was one-time; no subscription stream establishes long duration.
New annual payroll ₹17.02 crore plus software ₹4.85 crore are large against current revenue ₹51.37 crore.
DUR.contrary_fact: Recurring retainers and growing exports provide channels beyond proposed new products.

CAP.reason: NS: no meaningful incremental-reinvestment return or unit/cohort economics. Accounting ROIC cannot substitute.
supporting_facts: Human and software investments are expensed, and changing customer/vendor float distorts net invested capital.
The 65-hire/software program has no observed matured cohort contribution, retention-adjusted CAC or cash payback.
CAP.contrary_fact: Operating profits and retained value grew strongly; the positive arithmetic incremental ratio is evidence to investigate, not a validated marginal return.

CASH.reason: Persistent poor realization, not just one expansion year. The allowed GQS cap applies while GQS remains NS.
supporting_facts: Three-year CFO/PAT is 0.116× and four-year is 0.140×; FY2026 CFO is −₹1.10 crore.
Over-six-month AR is ₹2.603 crore; vendor advances and payable unwind absorbed cash.
CASH.contrary_fact: FY2025 CFO was positive ₹2.50 crore and ending AR days improved from 144 to 122.

BAL.reason: Dated balances and linked stress show funding fragility; current IPO availability is unverified.
supporting_facts: March cash ₹0.314 crore was small against ₹3.965 crore demand debt and statutory claims.
Conditional base minimum cash is ₹1.46 crore; a ₹5 crore resource drain makes it unfunded.
BAL.contrary_fact: Fresh net IPO proceeds of ₹29.87 crore potentially provide a substantial buffer; no actual default is established.

EXEC.reason: NS: historical growth is not evidence of delivery against the material new capital program.
supporting_facts: Headcount fell from 140 in FY2025 to 100 in June 2026; actual execution of 65 proposed hires is not verified.
Hiring/IT milestones are January/December 2027/2026 respectively and were not yet due; no reliable utilization report was located.
EXEC.contrary_fact: The company delivered ₹51.37 crore FY2026 sales and completed its IPO; lack of milestone evidence is not an evidenced failure.

EARN.reason: Profit growth is largely operating, but recurrence and the post-expansion expense base limit confidence. Cash realization is scored separately.
supporting_facts: Operating EBIT grew from ₹1.2225 to ₹11.1662 crore in FY2024–FY2026.
FY2026 EPS is ₹6.18 on current shares versus ₹8.40 on the historical weighted denominator.
EARN.contrary_fact: A FY2025 liability writeback and FY2026 deferred-tax credit require normalization, while new recurring costs are absent from old EPS.

R.reason: NS: a conditional return illustration is not a supported base forecast without current funding and cost-ramp evidence.
supporting_facts: Full-rollout base illustration gives terminal ₹75.08 and IRR −6.63%.
A ₹5 crore unknown intervening cash drain produces a funding gap and null ordinary IRR.
R.contrary_fact: Bull growth and cost improvement can produce 31.96% IRR, but that does not validate base resources or execution.

D.reason: Material permanent-loss risk under linked stress, tempered by discretionary cost reductions.
supporting_facts: A 25% sales loss and 42% ONWC produce an early funding gap under the new cost base.
Even the funded base terminal price is approximately 29% below entry before costs.
D.contrary_fact: IPO cash and the ability to defer unplaced hires/software may materially improve survival; modeled stress is not an actual default.

P.reason: The price requires growth and conversion to work together once the full recurring cost base is included.
supporting_facts: Correct post-IPO historical P/E is 17.13×, not 12.60× from old EPS.
At 12× terminal NOPAT the 15% hurdle requires constant 25.86% revenue growth and an 18.86% terminal EBIT margin.
P.contrary_fact: Historical growth exceeded this requirement, so expectations are demanding rather than impossible.

L.reason: NS: verified lot and secondary OHLCV bounds do not establish current execution or BSE restriction status.
supporting_facts: Five percent of the 20-day median volume is 720 shares, below the 1,200-share lot.
Only 40 listed sessions exist; three lots cost ₹380,880 and four cost ₹507,840.
L.contrary_fact: Observed trades exist and the SM interoperability row is eligible; the stock cannot be called suspended or untradeable from missing NSE trade data.
